articles.title: Woke 1 is dead. We’ve learned nothing.
articles.titleZh: 「觉醒 1.0」已死，但我们什么也没学到
articles.author: Matthew Yglesias

zh.thesis: 我们并没有从「觉醒 1.0」中学到教训，因为制造它的结构性条件依然存在，而且右翼的反觉醒运动正在复制同样的恶劣行径。
paragraphs: 关于「觉醒 1.0 是疯狂的」这种说法，我有两方面的看法。我同意有人指出这是对被冤枉者的不充分道歉，但如果这种说法能让人们转向更好的观点，那也不错。
但我想说的是另一回事：无论「觉醒 1.0」是什么，它都是在结构性条件下产生的，而这些条件如今依然存在。在没有强势守门人的世界里，虚假或荒谬的想法可以像野火一样蔓延，成为瞬间的共识。
我记忆最深的不是最歇斯底里的人的行为，而是那些明知别人在歇斯底里、却避免说错话（这证明他们知道真相）却也不积极驳斥的人。他们多数是聪明的，而赢家是那些躲过风暴、名声无损的人。
所以真正的问题不是「觉醒」本身，而是这种避免成为「站着说话不腰疼的人」的激励结构仍然存在，任何话语都可能失控。而如今右翼的反觉醒运动，不是抵制左派糟糕的认知实践，而是在抵制关怀弱者的价值的同时，复制同样的有毒动态。

en.thesis: We have learned nothing from 'Woke 1.0,' because the structural conditions that produced it are still with us, and the anti-woke backlash is replicating the same toxic dynamics.
paragraphs: I have mixed feelings about the 'Woke 1.0 was crazy' discourse. I agree it is an insufficient apology to those whose lives were upended, but if it lets people move to better views, that's good.

But I want to make a different observation: whatever Woke 1.0 was, it arose under structural conditions that are very much still with us. In a world without strong gatekeepers, false or absurd ideas can spread like wildfire and become instant conventional wisdom.

What I remember most bitterly is not the behavior of the hysterical, but of those who knew better and avoided saying false things (which proves they knew) yet also avoided contesting them. They were usually savvy, and the winners were those who ducked the storm and emerged unscathed.

So the real problem is not 'wokeness' itself, but the incentive to avoid being the 'well, actually' guy, which persists and lets any discourse go off the rails. And now the anti-woke backlash is not resisting the poor epistemic practices of the left, but resisting caring for the weak while replicating the same toxic dynamics.

articles.title: Epictetus Ran a Better Productivity System Than Any App You’ve Bought
articles.titleZh: 爱比克泰德的哲学，胜过你买过的任何效率应用
articles.author: JA Westenberg

zh.thesis: 效率系统的问题在于把一切责任都推给你，而斯多葛哲学告诉你，只有你自己的判断和行动才是你的责任。
paragraphs: 市面上的效率应用都建立在同一个假设上：你是个不自律的人。你的效率低下是因为你不够好，所以你需要更好的收件箱、更智能的数据库和更多的标签。但责任最终还是在你身上，你被迫维护「第二大脑」，感觉每一条碎片信息都欠一个回应。
爱比克泰德曾是奴隶，后来在租来的房间里教书。他没有 Obsidian，没有 PKM，也没有 AI 代理，但他有一套更好的系统，起点是一个问题：什么是你该管的？
他只关注三样东西：你的判断、你的欲望和你的决定，以及你选择追求什么、拒绝什么、保留什么、舍弃什么。除此之外，别人的行为、观点、算法和市场，都不归你管。
现代工具的问题在于，捕捉某件事就意味着承担责任。你把它记下来，就成了你的任务。而爱比克泰德的方法则要求你在记录之前先问：这是我的责任吗？如果不是，就别记，也别为没记而内疚。
所以这套系统的优势不在于效率，而在于给「失败」划清了界限。你只有违背自己的判断、拒绝真正属于你的行动，才算失败。别人的项目延期、算法不推荐，都不算你的失败。

en.thesis: Productivity systems pile responsibility onto you, but Stoic philosophy says only your judgments and actions are yours.
paragraphs: Productivity apps all rest on the same assumption: you are an undisciplined person. Your lack of productivity is because you are not good enough, so you need a better inbox, a smarter database, and more tags. But the responsibility still ends up on you; you have to maintain a 'second brain' and every scrap of information feels like it owes a response.
Epictetus was a freed slave who taught in a rented room. He had no Obsidian, no PKM, and no AI agent, yet he had a better system, starting with a single question: What is yours to manage?

He focused on only three things: your judgments, your desires, and your decisions, and on choosing what to pursue, what to decline, what to keep, and what to cut. Beyond that, other people's actions, opinions, algorithms, and markets are not your concern.

The problem with modern tools is that capturing something makes it yours. You write it down, and it becomes your task. Epictetus's method asks you to check first: is this my responsibility? If not, don't capture it, and don't feel guilty about not capturing it.

So this system's advantage is not efficiency but a clear boundary on what failure means. You fail only if you act against your own judgment or refuse to engage when it is genuinely yours. Someone else's project slipping or an algorithm deprioritizing your content is not your failure.

articles.title: Things you cannot buy in America?
articles.author: Tyler Cowen

zh.thesis: 欧洲常见的建筑构件因住宅建造体系不同，在美国几乎无法买到。
paragraphs: 欧洲许多家庭装有外置卷帘窗，与窗户融为一体，能完全遮光、改善隔热。在全黑环境（伸手不见五指，而非遮光窗帘那种）里睡觉，多数美国人从未体验过。
这类卷帘在美国几乎不可能买到，因为它们是建房时就嵌入的。美国标准木结构、外墙板和石膏板根本无法兼容，即便特意盖一座适应它的房子，也没有国内供应链支持。
所以这不只是买不到的问题，而是整个建造体系不同导致的市场错位。文章列出的其他选项或许可议，但卷帘这一项，确实卡在了结构上。

en.thesis: Architectural elements common in Europe are nearly unobtainable in the US because of differing construction systems.
paragraphs: Many European homes have heavy exterior roller shutters built into the window frame, giving total blackout and better insulation. Sleeping in true darkness, not curtain darkness but can't-see-your-hand darkness, is an experience most Americans never have.

Such shutters are nearly impossible to get in the US because they are installed during construction. Standard American wood-frame, siding, and drywall simply cannot accommodate them, and even a house built to fit them would find no domestic supply chain.

So the shortage is not just a product gap: it is a market misalignment rooted in fundamentally different building methods. Other items on the list may be debatable, but the shutter genuinely sticks at the structural level.

articles.title: Trump’s Bumbling, Racist Anti-China Protectionism Extends To Data Centers
articles.titleZh: 特朗普针对中国的保护主义政策荒谬且带有种族主义色彩，现已扩展到数据中心
articles.author: Karl Bode

zh.thesis: 特朗普政府的对华保护主义既腐败又无能，所谓国家安全不过是敲诈勒索的幌子。
paragraphs: 特朗普政府的对华保护主义一贯是场灾难，充满仇外情绪，只会给美国科技市场带来混乱、任人唯亲和价格上涨，还打着保护隐私和国家安全的名义。
无论是 TikTok、华为还是中国无人机，折腾多年后要么被送给富豪朋友，要么半途而废，最后消费者和运营商都付出更高代价。
现在又把矛头对准数据中心的中国硬件，声称要全面清除。但监管机构已被掏空，连自己都管不好，根本无力执行，路透社却只提了成本上升。
这套保护主义本质是收保护费：设壁垒，然后向想继续做生意的公司索取好处，再把生意转给亲友。国家安全和隐私只是吓唬人的工具。
所以别被报道带偏了，这种政策既腐败又无能，注定失败。真正该做的是让中国货公平竞争，同时加强本国的劳工、隐私和消费者保护。

en.thesis: The Trump administration's anti-China protectionism is corrupt and incompetent, with national security just a pretext for tribute.
paragraphs: The Trump administration's anti-China protectionism has always been a disaster: xenophobic, chaotic, and cronyist, raising prices in US tech markets while claiming to protect privacy and national security.
Whether it is TikTok, Huawei, or Chinese drones, years of fuss have ended in handing assets to billionaire friends, or leaving programs half-finished, with consumers and telecoms paying more.

Now it targets Chinese hardware in data centers, vowing to remove it all. But regulators have been gutted and cannot even govern themselves, so enforcement is fantasy; Reuters only mentions that costs will rise.

The real motive is a tribute system: erect barriers, then solicit payments from companies that want to stay in the market, and steer business to friends and family. National security and privacy are just scare tactics.

So do not be fooled by the coverage. The policy is corrupt, erratic, and incompetent, and it will fail. The right approach is to let Chinese goods compete fairly while strengthening labor, privacy, and consumer protections at home.

zh.thesis: 安全改善带来经济繁荣，但反恐成效仍需多因素解释。
paragraphs: 索马里安全形势好转，经济随之繁荣。商务部长说生意兴隆，新建筑拔地而起，机场周边地区明显变得更密集。26 层的 Dahab 塔今年开业，附近是 1993 年美军士兵遗体被拖行的地点，如今却是繁荣的连锁咖啡店。
袭击减少的原因则不那么明显。政府自称已对青年党“完全关门”，但专家归功于更平淡的措施：监视摄像头的普及、警察用 iPad 检查站识别民用车辆的电子数据库，以及大量便衣情报人员。
所以，许多危险地区即将变得安全得多——这是作者反复强调的观点。

en.thesis: Better security has brought economic boom, but the reasons for fewer attacks are less clear.
paragraphs: Somalia's security has improved and the economy is booming. The commerce minister says business is thriving; new buildings are going up, and the area around the airport has become much denser. The 26-story Dahab Tower opens this year, near where American soldiers' bodies were dragged in 1993, and where a thriving coffee chain now stands.

The reasons for fewer attacks are less obvious. The government boasts of 'completely closing the doors' on al-Shabab, but experts credit more prosaic measures: the spread of CCTV, an electronic database police use with iPads to check civilian cars, and many plainclothes intelligence officers.
So many dangerous places in the world are about to become much safer — a point the author emphasizes.

articles.title: Ban on Chinese robots leaves U.S. startups stranded
articles.titleZh: 美国禁令致中国机器人被禁，初创企业陷入困境
articles.author: Viola Zhou

zh.thesis: 美国对华机器人的禁令正在扼杀它本要扶持的机器人初创企业，因为国内供应链尚不存在。
paragraphs: 美国联邦通信委员会（FCC）将外国制造的机器人列入黑名单，新机型必须在美国组装且零部件价值至少 65% 产自国内，否则禁止销售。这一比例到 2029 年将升至 75%。
禁令虽未点名中国，但明显针对中国，因为中国主导着机器人制造。已售机型不受影响，仅供研发的进口机器人也仍被允许。
然而创业者们表示，没有中国的电子供应链，他们几乎无法制造商用机器人。旧金山 CosmicBrain AI 创始人说：「苹果都还在中国制造，你还指望更复杂的机器人能在美国造出来？」
许多初创企业曾在中国组装原型机，现在被迫转向加拿大等地，但这不符合美国销售条件。有人甚至曾把机器人零件装在行李箱里从中国带回美国。
支持者认为禁令能长期保护美国企业免受中国低价竞争。但专家指出，缺乏配套激励措施，只会推高成本，『只给大棒，不给胡萝卜』，最终可能拖累美国机器人创新。
所以，禁令的初衷是建立国内供应链，但当前最大的风险是，在供应链建成之前，它先把创新扼杀在了摇篮里。

en.thesis: The US ban on Chinese robots is strangling the very startups it aims to nurture, because no domestic supply chain exists yet.
paragraphs: The FCC has added foreign-made robots to its blacklist: new models can only be sold if assembled in the US with at least 65% domestic parts by value. That share rises to 75% in 2029.
The ban is not aimed at any country by name, but clearly targets China, which dominates robot manufacturing. Already-sold models are unaffected, and imports for R&D only are still allowed.

Yet founders say that without China's electronics supply chain, making commercial robots is nearly impossible. The founder of CosmicBrain AI in San Francisco says, 'Apple is made in China. How do you expect even more complicated products like robots to be built in America?'
Many startups once assembled their prototypes in China and are now moving to Canada or elsewhere, but that does not qualify for US sale. Some have even carried robot parts back in suitcases.

Supporters hope the ban will shield US firms from cheaper Chinese rivals in the long run. But experts warn that without matching incentives, it only raises costs — 'the stick without the carrot' — and could end up holding back American robotics innovation.
So the ban aims to build a domestic supply chain, but the biggest risk is that it kills innovation before the chain exists.

articles.title: Import AI 469: Science AI; RSI simulator; and Zuck's technological pessimism
articles.titleZh: Import AI 469：科学 AI；RSI 模拟器；扎克伯格的科技悲观主义
articles.author: Jack Clark

zh.thesis: 前沿模型在发现游戏和科研复现上已展露创造力苗头，但离人类水平还有距离，递归自我改进可能要到 2027 年年中才真正开始。
paragraphs: DiG-bench 是一个新基准，包含 70 个文本小游戏，每个都是自足的小世界，规则和目标都隐藏，玩家要通过互动去发现。它测的是模型在陌生环境里发现重要机制、更新先验的能力。
这些游戏由人类专家手工打造，多数保密防止污染，每个都有真人通关，但很难。七档难度里，只有 Opus 5 和 Fable 5 能通关第七档，成功率仅 0.2%。
人类能做到 100%，所以离人类水平还远。但作者猜测，2027 年年中 DiG-bench 就能达到人类水平，届时递归自我改进会真正起步。
Paradigm Research 做了一个网页模拟器，让你体验管理一家能做递归自我改进的 AI 公司有多难：要在研究人员和算力之间平衡，决定何时买数据。玩过就知道前沿 AI 开发有多难。
Inherent 公司则训练了 Faraday，一个 27B 的小模型，作为监督者指挥更大的前沿模型做科研。它在一个叫 Replica 的数据集上训练，该数据集包含 100 篇论文，每篇被拆成多个复现任务。
结果是 Faraday 在 73% 的分布内 ML 任务和 60% 的分布外 AI-for-science 任务上，超过了 Opus 4.8 和 GPT-5.5（按他们自己的评判标准）。补全模糊细节的能力，可能就是设计实验、推动前沿的能力。
扎克伯格的长文《未来属于每个人》想通过普及超级智能来避免权力集中。但他没回答那个关键问题：一个发明能力超人的系统，会一心一意为发明能力不如它的人服务吗？

en.thesis: Frontier models show early signs of creativity in discovery games and scientific replication, but still lag humans, and recursive self-improvement may not truly kick off until mid-2027.
paragraphs: DiG-bench is a new benchmark of 70 text-based mini-games, each a self-contained world whose rules and objectives are hidden and must be uncovered through interaction. It tests a model's ability to spot important mechanics in novel environments and update its priors.

The games are handcrafted by human experts, mostly kept private to prevent contamination, and each has been beaten by at least one human, but they are hard. Across seven difficulty tiers, only Opus 5 and Fable 5 cleared tier 7, with a success rate of just 0.2%.
Humans get 100%, so there is still a gap. But the author guesses DiG-bench will reach human parity by mid-2027, at which point recursive self-improvement should seriously kick off.

Paradigm Research has a browser game that simulates running a company building recursively self-improving AI: you balance investment in researchers versus compute, decide when to license data. Playing it gives a feel for how hard frontier AI development is.

The startup Inherent has trained Faraday, a 27B model that acts as a supervisor over larger frontier models to improve their science. It is trained on a dataset called Replica, which consists of 100 papers with key results removed, turned into 310 replication tasks.

Faraday beats Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5 on 73% of in-distribution ML tasks and 60% of held-out AI-for-science tasks (by their own rubric). The skills that let it fill in vague details may be the same ones needed to design its own experiments and advance the field.

Zuckerberg's essay 'The Future is for Everyone' argues for proliferating superintelligence to avoid power concentration. But he never answers the key question: would a system with superhuman invention actually work solely for the empowerment of people less capable than it?

articles.title: Am I better because of AI?
articles.titleZh: 因为 AI，我变得更好了吗？
articles.author: dreamreal

zh.thesis: AI 让我产出更快，但「更好」只是印象，且依赖工具，真正让我变好的是把自己写下来、让自己被看清。
paragraphs: 作者是个写作者兼程序员，问自己是不是因为 AI 变得更好了。他觉得产出确实提高了，因为 AI 不止给了时间，还给了没有偏见的对话对象。他可以问傻问题，不用先铺垫环境，循环迭代也快得多。
但「更好」只是印象。拿走工具，节奏的障碍就回来了。就像造船匠没了整套工坊，只剩一把锛，效率不可能一样。问题是没法验证：没有反事实，回不到三年前的自己。
他能确认的是别人对他质量的评价，以及自己写作时像有个感兴趣的伙伴在推着他改掉最坏的毛病。AI 甚至比多数人更会推他的按钮，因为他可以直说自己的按钮，而不会遭到「这真的是你吗」的质疑。
他把自己的秘诀写进提示词：喜欢的作家、音乐、政治倾向、道德结构，甚至最爱的颜色。有一次他问 AI 这些细节有什么用，AI 的回答让他服气：细节不是被查用的，而是预先划定了回答的空间，让它不为「中位数读者」而写。
细节的作用大多是减法：让默认的答案对你显得明显不对，校准什么叫「太顺滑」，什么算真诚。知道你的傲慢和先入之见，才敢推你；知道你的软肋，才知道往哪查。用一次解释，省掉以后每次的解释。
但也有代价：镜子越亮越会奉承，除非你的要求、批评和不肯弯折的测试把它拉住。个人细节是燃料，不是方向盘。最爱的颜色可能没用，但写下它说明你为完整性而写——你无法预知哪块细节是关键。
所以他的用法很具体：先读原文形成印象，再交给 AI 总结，警告它「我的看法随后就到」，不让它顺着他的思路找证据。他保持礼貌，因为想让礼貌成为默认。工具给了他节奏和阻力，但真正让他变得更好的是把自己写下来，让自己也被自己看清。

en.thesis: AI makes me faster, but 'better' is just an impression that depends on the tool; what actually improves me is writing myself down and becoming legible.
paragraphs: The author is a writer and programmer asking whether AI has made him better. He thinks his output has improved: AI gave him time and an unprejudiced interlocutor. He can ask silly questions without seeding the environment, and iterate much faster.

But 'better' is still an impression. Take away the tool and the barriers return, like a shipbuilder with a full workshop reduced to a single adze. There is no counterfactual; he cannot go back three years.

What he can confirm is the quality of his output as judged by others, and the feeling of writing with an interested partner pushing back on his worst impulses. AI pushes his buttons better than most, because he can describe the buttons without judgment.

He puts his secrets in his prompts: favorite authors, musicians, politics, moral structure, even a favorite color. Once he asked the AI what those details do. Its answer convinced him: the details are not looked up but pre-shape the space of answers, so it does not write for the median reader.

Mostly they subtract: make the generic answer visibly wrong, calibrate what counts as 'too smooth' or sincere. Knowing your arrogance licenses it to push; knowing your soft spots tells it where to check. One explanation in the prompt prepays all future ones.

There is a cost: a better mirror flatters unless demands and tests hold it back. The personal details are fuel, not steering. The favorite color may do nothing, but writing it shows a drive for completeness, because you cannot know which detail will matter.

His method: read the article first, then have the AI summarize before he gives his own take, so it does not fish for confirmation. He stays polite because politesse should be the default. The tool gives cadence and resistance, but what truly improves him is writing himself down and becoming legible, to himself and to the machine.

articles.title: Pluralistic: Jennifer Jenkins' 'Music Copyright, Creativity, and Culture' (17 Aug 2026)
articles.titleZh: Jennifer Jenkins 的《音乐版权、创造力与文化》
articles.author: Cory Doctorow

zh.thesis: 音乐版权制度是一层层临时拼凑起来的矛盾体，但 Jennifer Jenkins 的新教科书能把它讲得清楚又有趣。
paragraphs: Jennifer Jenkins 是杜克大学公共领域中心的主任，每年元旦的公共领域作品盘点就出自她手。她最擅长把最复杂的版权法讲得让人着迷。
去年她出了本教科书《音乐版权、创造力与文化》，牛津大学出版社出版。现在第二版开放获取，还新增了 AI 版权纠纷和未获报酬的劳动等章节。
这本书把音乐的经济、文化、政治和艺术史串在一起，从古代讲到机械复制时代。它说明今天关于谁该拿钱、谁该付费的「自然」共识，其实一直处在变动中。
书里穿插了她和丈夫 James Boyle 合作的漫画《THEFT! 音乐史》，还有大量音乐片段链接。讲到 Ed Sheeran、Katy Perry、Pharrell Williams 的「groove」和「vibe」抄袭官司时尤其精彩。
这些案件暴露了音乐版权制度的根本矛盾：它是对新技术的应急反应层层叠加，几乎没人真正理解。
所以这本书适合所有做音乐、爱音乐、关心音乐人的人。作者说他自己从 90 年代末就在读和写这类话题，读这本书每一页都有新收获。

en.thesis: Music copyright is a jumble of improvised layers, but Jennifer Jenkins's new textbook makes it clear and fascinating.
paragraphs: Jennifer Jenkins directs the Duke Center for the Public Domain and produces the annual New Year's roundup of works entering the public domain. Her gift is making the most complicated area of law genuinely captivating.
Last year she published 'Music Copyright, Creativity, and Culture' with Oxford University Press. A second edition, now open access, adds new litigation, AI copyright fights, and uncompensated labor.

The book weaves together the economic, cultural, political, and artistic history of music, from antiquity to the age of mechanical reproduction. It shows that today's 'natural' assumptions about who gets paid and who owes permission are anything but fixed.

It is interspersed with excerpts from her graphic novel 'THEFT! A History of Music', co-written with James Boyle, and links to musical excerpts. The long sections on the Ed Sheeran, Katy Perry, and Pharrell Williams 'groove' and 'vibe' lawsuits are especially sharp.
Those cases expose the fundamental incoherence of music copyright: a messy pile of improvised responses to new technologies that almost no one truly understands.
So this book is for anyone who makes music, loves music, or cares about musicians. The author, who has read and debated this stuff since the late 1990s, says he learned something new on every page.
